div.head:
THE COMMENTARY OF DIONYSIOS BAR SALIBI ON
THE BOOK OF MICAH

div.ab: The interpretation of the prophecy of Micha, literally. Micah prophesied in the time of Hosea, Joel, and Amos, and in the days of the Kings Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. And he said:

div.head: Chapter 1
div.ab: 1) The word of the Lord: i.e., revelations.
2) Hear, all ye peoples: i.e., he calls the tribes peoples, i.e., the two kingdoms. Hearken O earth: i.e., let the promised land hear.

3) For behold, the Lord: i.e., issues from the mount Zion, where he dwells. And comes down and treads upon the height of the land: i.e., that of the promise. He
treads its inhabitants under him, the kings and nobles.

4) And the valleys: i.e., the common people; that is to say, the entire populace shall be molten like wax. And like waters that run down: i.e., that descend. (By) a slope: i.e., from the height. Thus they are being forcibly led by the captors.
5) What is the transgression of Jacob: i.e.,but that you worshipped the idols that are in Samaria. Thus also of Juda; the idols that are in Jerusalem.

6) I will make Jerusalem: i.e., because of these sins Jerusalem will be destroyed and become a site for common use for the seed of every species.
And I will pile up her stones: i.e., the ploughmen will uproot all her habitations from her foundations and will pile up her stones in a heap, that she may the more readily be used for cultivation by the plough, for the casting of the seed, and for the planting of the vineyard.

7) For from the wages of the harlot came the idols, i.e., as wages to the demons with whom they committed fornication. And to the wages of the harlot, that they should come, calling wages the punishment that they will receive.
9) And it is come unto Judah: i.e., to these two tribes also, the lamentation of mourning is coming and being transmitted.

10) At Gath do ye not rejoice: i.e., do not rejoice, ye children of Jerusalem, over the idols of Gath that were led away captive, as if you would inherit their land. For you also will be led away captive. And weep ye not at all: i.e., over them, but weep over yourselves, for not for weeping nor for rejoicing are ye left. In the houses of Ūphra: the city of Gideon. Sprinkle yourselves with dust:
i.e., ye Israelites, through repentance, lest on the contrary it happen to you. By the single city of Ūphra he speaks about their entire land.

11) Do (or make) for thyself, inhabitant (feminine): i.e., behold I, myself have threatened these things in advance. Now thou, oh inhabitant (feminine) of Israel. Do for thyself... that which is comely (or good): i.e., either through repentance or through some other means for your help. Naked didst thou go forth: i.e., naked didst thou go forth before the captors, inhabitants (fem.) of Israel, that didst formerly dwell in Zoan, when they were in Egypt. The lamentation of Beth ʾŌsel: i.e., you will suffer a grievous affliction, comparable to those of the city of ʾŌsel taking from you comfort for themselves so that more grievous than (theirs is) the affliction which has come upon you.

12) Because she wearied toward the good: i.e., she was wearying and falling into the punishment of captivity, because she had wearied and weakened toward the doing of good, and had rebelled against God and against the prophets. Unto the gates of Jerusalem: i.e., I, the Lord, who am mocked by them, I move and bring unto Jerusalem the chariots and the horses of the Babylonians.

13) The inhabitant of Lachish: i.e., from her began the cult of wickedness, and it was transferred to the Jerusalemites. The inhabitants of Lachish were the cause for the error of Baal and of the calf of the ten tribes seizing upon these two tribes. Others say that he upbraids Lachish for this, that Amaziah, King of Judah, was killed there (in her), i.e., she was the first to kill a king in the kingdom of Judah after the manner of the kingdom of the ten tribes.

14) And therefore thou shalt give up claim, i.e., (to) the inheritance that you had acquired from the Philistines shall be left behind by you in captivity. But he does not say that you will leave your land and the Philistines will come and inherit it, because before them they had been carried into captivity by the Assyrians.

16) Pluck out and shave.... like an eagle: i.e., it is meet for you that you suffer bitterly when you are in captivity. And as the eagle in his old age sheds his moulting, thus also you, when the time the Lord has decreed for you comes, will shed all your finery by the hands of thy enemies.

div.head: Chapter 2
div.ab: 6) Do not weep: i.e., do not weep over these distresses which come upon you, only over your sins weep and cry.

7) They had provoked his spirit: i.e., they had embittered his will. Behold my words are doing good: i.e., this will be to you a demonstration that I am able to do any miracle. For as my good words were accomplished and fulfilled to your forefathers, thus also my words concerning the captivity and my threats through the prophets will come and be fulfilled upon you.

8) My people like a thief: i.e., like a thief who continually resists those who counsel to him peace and who prepares himself for evil, thus also this nation was rising against God and against the prophets who were counseling to it peace and good (deeds). His skin you will strip: i.e., on account of those things what will happen to the nation the Assyrians will strip its skin. Who remove, cause to pass away: i.e., the riches, he who robbed the poor, while he was trusting and hope
that he would enjoy its possession. And who bring back war: i.e., you, Israelites, through your transgression you brought upon yourselves war so that the enemies come again and fight with you.
10) Because of the pollution: i.e., that pollution that you cultivated in this land which he calls a rest, it (the land) will do you harm and cause you to perish.

11) A man who walks.... and drunkenness: i.e., a false prophet who walks with falsehood (treachery) and in the spirit of deceit, he distilled upon you punishment and intoxicated you. Wine: he calls the punishment which nauseates and intoxicates, like (the word): a cup is in the Lord's hand. (Psalm 75:8). And it will be like: i.e., of the very same chastisement with which the people are smitten, will overflow like a distillation also on the prophets who led it astray.

12) All of thee Jacob: i.e., although they are going now to take refuge with the Egyptians or to gentiles in other places they will gain nothing, because I myself am about to gather them from the dispersion to Jerusalem. And I will
make it like a flock.... from men: i.e., they will be besieged within Jerusalem by the Babylonians and they will be crowded together like a flock crowded in the fold and hidden, that is to say, deprived of guardians and shepherds, and if the lion or the bear comes he destroys the whole flock.

13) A destroyer came up: i.e., the Babylonians who shatter the wall of Jerusalem before the Jews and lead them out into captivity. And the Lord at the head of them: It is because of this the Babylonians were able to do these (things), because the Lord was coming at the head of the camp of the Babylonians and was making war with the Jews.

div.head: Chapter 3
div.ab: 5) Concerning the false prophets: They proclaim against it war, i.e., he warns against the false prophets and says that against whatever does not bring them bread they prophesy evil.

6) Therefore night, all of it: i.e., he says that God is bringing upon them a darkness of distress in which they will be while nothing will appear to them or be found out by them for their deliverance.

8) But truly, I am full: i.e., the prophet sets forth his distinction from the false prophets. I am full: i.e., I am not like they, but I am full of the holy spirit. And from it I have acquired heroic power which does not slacken,
12) And the mountain of the house (shall become) a forest: i.e., the Temple with the hill on which it is built shall be devastated, and trees will grow upon it like on a desolate mountain.

div.head: Chapter 4
div.ab:
1) The mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established on the top of the mountains and shall be higher than the hills: i.e., according to custom of the prophets into the midst of depressing (statements) he mingles gladdening words. In the last days of the return, when all the
Jews will be gathered to Jerusalem, this mountain of Zion on which the house of the Lord is built, which is higher and more glorious than all the mountains of the world, and made unshakeably firm by that power which dwells upon it, by the divine providence will become known to everybody.

3) And it (the word) shall judge among the nations: i.e., he will judge and reprove many nations who are distant and afar. He refers to the house of Gog. And they shall beat their swords: i.e., when those of the house of Gog will be destroyed then all the nations will change their weapons to husbandry, for they will no longer possess knowledge of the war against the Jews.

8) And Thou, O Tower, shepherd: i.e., after the other things which he has said about the return, he threatens them again. Tower, he calls Jerusalem, because of the Temple which is in it. And a kingdom (he calls her), because she shepherds and directs them. Dark he calls her because she is darkened with idols, and the light of the fear of God has been divorced from her. Your time has come: i.e., that you descend to Babylon in captivity. And a ruler has come: i.e., he calls Nebuchadnezzar ruler because Nebuchadnezzar had already come, to establish his rule over you and to subjugate you.
First he calls him because of his greatness and power, and because his is the first of all in his rule.

10) Suffer birth pangs and labor: i.e., bear the birth pangs which deservedly attain you and labor (with them), if you would excel like a pregnant woman, who, when she gives birth labors with the pains and is delivered. For a short time even you also will suffer these things, and afterwards you will be released from them.

11) Henceforth will be gathered against Thee: i.e., he says concerning the house of Gog and those who came up with them after the return. Let Zion be defiled: i.e., because they were expecting that they would defile the sanctuary of Zion and see the destruction of Jerusalem through the destruction which they were about to perform there.

div.head: Chapter 5
div.ab:
1) Henceforth you will go forth in raiding-troops: i.e., you will go forth and raid all those who come to raid you. Strong raiding troops he calls Abraham, Moses, Joshua, and David, because of their leadership, that is, in war. They rose up against me and smote: i.e., such was their readiness, that they will smite me (read us) severely upon our
cheeks with a rod, us with the head of our nation.

2) But thou, Bethlehem: i.e., now he tells about him who is to be the leader of the war. From Thee shall go forth: i.e., even though you, Bethlehem, are small in power and in number in comparison with the enemies, and not sufficient to stand among the hands of thousands of Juda as of yore, yet for God this is not difficult to destroy in a moment the whole multitude of enemies by this(word). From thee shall go forth: i.e., your king, Zerubabel; for from you he is about to go forth and conquer those of the house of Gog. His going forth (is) from the beginning: i.e., these (words) refer to the Messiah for Zerubabel was born in the time of the captivity and not from the beginning and the days of yore.

3) And he will deliver them up.... A travailing woman: i.e., he calls Jerusalem a travailing woman because she is in distress, as though in birth pangs, and expects that a Saviour will be born to her and her birth pangs relieved. And he says that henceforth he will deliver them up to the distresses of the captivity, until the time when the return shall be brought forth, that is, until they will return from captivity these things are to be fulfilled. Spiritually God
will dliver them up to oppressions, until the Messiah shall be born in flesh. And the rest of his brothers will return: i.e., when they will not be divided into two kingdoms as formerly, but like brothers they will subject themselves to one head who is Zerubabel.
4) Because henceforth.... of the land: i.e., and from the great things which the Lord accomplished at the return. Thereupon he will become great and his name will be glorified all over the world.

5) And there shall be peace: i.e., when Gog has fallen, we shall obtain peace forever. And the Assyrian, when he comes: i.e., because these things were remote, as for their confirmation he adduces those things which were fulfilled in the case of Hezekiah and at that very time. We shall raise against him seven shepherds. i.e., take this indication to yourselves, that the Lord will destroy the house of Gog, from this that he is about to destroy also the Assyrians and his host in the punishment. And concerning the seven shepherds and the eight princes, it indicates the complete, full and abundant mishap that attained the Assyrians through the angel, according to the idiom: give the portion, seven, even eight (which means in full). Others say, the seven shepherds are the
prophets who before the coming up of the Assyrian were prophesying his fall. Eight: i.e., kings. Hezekiah and those with him, namely the nobles.
6) They shall attack the land of the Assyrians: i.e., I am about to raise the Babylonians against the Assyrian, and they are coming and destroy the land and the kingdom which is corrupted by Nimrod.

7) And the (remnant) shall be, i.e., before the Lord, i.e., when the Assyrian has fallen, those who remained over in Jerusalem; God will show them to be pitiable to all nations like dew when it falls upon the earth, and like fine rain.... to man, i.e., as dew or fine rain when it is taken up; i.e., when men try to take it up to drink or use it in any way, does not abide nor tarry for any one, thus also those from among the nations, who had fled and he who had sought refuge with them (perhaps the nations) are to return to Jerusalem when the Assyrian has fallen and fled to his place.
9) Thine hand shall be lifted up: i.e., Hezekiah. Against your haters and all your enemies: i.e., the Assyrians, shall perish.
10) I will destroy thy horses out of the midst of Thee: i.e., he prophesies concerning the punishment which he is bringing upon Assyria through the Babylonians.
14) Your groves: i.e., those groves in which the Assyrians used to worship the idols.

div.head: Chapter 6
div.ab: 1) Rise, litigate Thou upon the mountains: i.e., he prophesies again concerning those things that are to come upon Jerusalem through the Babylonians. Arise, thou prophet, and litigate upon the mountains and the heights which are round about Jerusalem, which received the corpses of the Assyrians and let them know that they shall assemble to the court of the Lord. And the mute things (i.e., the mountains and hills) shall hear instead of those gifted with perception, and the silent things shall reprove those gifted with speech, who have made themselves deafmutes.
2) For the Lord is about to litigate: He reproves it (the people) concerning its graceless iniquity.

3) My people: i.e., he represents it (the people) for the kindnesses it enjoyed from the time of Egypt, and it
is found unthankful for kindnesses.

5) What counsel he sought: i.e., he reminds it (the people) of the case of Balak when he sought to destroy the nation through Balaam's curse. And what Balaam answered him: i.e., at first, and I restrained him and turned the curses into blessings. From Shatim: i.e., when the camp (of Israel) was spread out from Shatim up to Gilgal, from the head of the camp to its end. For he knows (Peshitta has knew): i.e., even Balaam himself knew the righteousness of the Lord which (was) in the midst of the people and he did not deem it right that it should be cursed.

6) Wherewith shall I come before the Lord: i.e., when the prophet appears as the advocate for the people, he says these things as if in their person. And I shall be pleasing: i.e., for I saw in all the cases it appeared that I was ungrateful for kindnesses.

7) And the Lord will not be pleased: i.e., this the prophet answers to the people. Shall I offer my firstborn? i.e., and at once the prophet says this in the person of the people. You will do justice: i.e., the prophet declares immediately what is much to offer. And Thou shalt love goodness: i.e., mercy to the poor. And you shall be ready to go: i.e., give up the notion that through sacrifices you shall please God, and take heed of that which Moses has commanded
love toward the Lord and love toward the neighbors.

9) Hear ye, rod, what he testifies: i.e., who will testify that you are the stock and inheritance of God. For as it is impossible for fire (vs. 10) to be placed on pieces of wood without kindling them, thus also is it impossible that the wickedness (vs. 10) which has been heaped up in your houses, like in storehouses (vs. 10) should not kindle you. More than fire pieces of wood will wickedness kindle its doers. And still more you, who in storehouses of wickedness and in weights (vs. 11) and measures (vs. 10) of wickedness, have multiplied your transgression. The pouch (vs. 11) is equivalent to a small bag and the weights are put into it.

14) And a dysentery shall be: i.e., the divine anger shall pass through your land by means of the enemies, who has dysentery in his belly. Everything he eats does not stay within, and his appetite is not satiated, thus shall it be with everything you possess. Thou shalt attain: i.e.,
also the good things which you attain will be taken away by the enemies, and you will not be able to save them.

16) And the reproach of my people: i.e., the punishment for its reproach and its blasphemy against God that the people will receive, that everyone who sees it (him) will reproach it, (saying) that on account of its sins it suffers all these things.

div.head: Chapter 7
div.ab:
1) Woe is me that I have become: i.e., the prophet himself took on (in his own person, though he did not really show it) in their suffering and laments for them on their being diverted from good to bad. Like the gathering of the summer: Woe is me, what is this which I see in this people, that when it was diligently served with the good things that are from God, it was sated with fruits of the best kinds, and
(now) like a farmer who expects to collect fruit at the time when the fruits are gone it gathers and brings together a little bit. And my soul desires the first ripe fruit: i.e., he calls the first of the fruit the first ripe fruit, and says that he longs sorely to find among them a man fit for the divine will, like a cluster of grapes.
3) And the great man speaks: i.e., the king speaks those (very words) that urge the people to bring him a bribe speaks, and not according to the divine laws.
4) The day of your watchman: i.e., mocking he says this, that the day has arrived when according to the indications of the false prophets you are saved.

7) But I will look unto the Lord: i.e., as in their person (i.e., as personifying them) he says: At the time of the return, however, I: i.e., although I am surrounded by evil things like these, I do not give up the hope of my salvation; but seeing God I trust that he hears me and relieves my distresses.

8) Rejoice not over me: i.e., he calls to Edom, the enemy: Although I have fallen in captivity, I will
rise again in the return.

10) They shall look at her: i.e., he hints at the destruction which was to attain the Edomites after the return on the part of the people. She shall be for a treading-down: i.e., she shall be trodden down by the enemies like the mud of the streets by passers-by of the road.

11) A day for the building: he refers to the return; your walls will be rebuilt that you may dissolve your enemies. When thou (feminine) shalt be taken up: i.e., the day is near when thou (feminine) shalt be taken up on the shoulders of the nation and return to Jerusalem. The Greek has the opposite of this meaning:- That day on which you will be walled in by the enemies: And you will be carried away from your land through captivity.

17) They shall lick the dust: i.e., he said this concerning the nations, who at the destruction of the House of Gog will be humbled and lowered; And like moles: i.e., they will hide themselves in the ground from fear, like moles and serpents, who, when they hear the voice of a man turn back and do not creep any more into their places; thus also the nations, when they see what happens to the House of Gog will turn back from preparation for war. They shall be angered:
i.e., desisting from their undertaking, which was prepared out of anger.
The literal interpretation of the prophet Mica is finished.

noteGrp.note: p. 15, n. 1 For the convenience of the reader the writer has included the chapter and verse numbers. They are not given by Bar Salibi. The Hebrew text of the rabbinic parallels given in the translation will be found in the Appendix, pp. 36 ff.
p. 15, n. 2 Kimchi's comment on t is verse Hear all ye people, is that this statement refers to Israel, and the plural of nation refers to the tribes.
p. 15, n. 3 Kimchi explains the land as meaning land of Israel.
p. 15, n. 4 Ibn Ezra designates the place from which he departs saying: He was in his holy temple, etc.
p. 16, n. 1 Ibn Ezra comments: And tread upon the high places of the earth. Others say that: the high places of the earth refer to the rulers, etc.
p. 16, n. 2 Kimchi states: And the valleys is an illustration of the vanishing of the populace.
p. 16, n. 3 Kimchi's comment is similar: Like waters which pour down from a precipice and flow in every direction, so will the (Children of Israel) be scattered in the lands of the Gentiles.

p. 16, n. 4 Kimchi makes a similar statement: What is the cause for the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria which was the capital of the kingdom? It was the source of idol worship and the dwelling place of the Baal prophets who deterred Israel from the Lord. And what are the high places of Judah? Is not Jerusalem the capital of the kingdom which was the first to set up altars for idol worship? From it the other cities of Judah learned it.

p. 16, n. 5 All the available texts of the Peshitta version read like the Masoritic text: Samaria. Changes in text by Bar Salibi are frequent. Here Bar Salibi quoted from memory and because the preceding verse ends with the word Jerusalem he quotes by error the word Jerusalem instead of Samaria. Cf. The Commentary of Dionysios Bar Salibi on the Book of Amos, Dissertation by Herbert Gordon May, June, 1930. P. 90.

p. 17, n. 1 Kimchi comments on The hire of an harlot as follows: They used to present the idols with whom they committed adultery with silver and gold and beautiful garments in the same way as the hire of an harlot.

p. 17, n. 2 Professor Sprengling suggests that it is possible that the word (rejoice) used by Bar Salibi and the Peshitta for the word (announce) which corresponds to the correct Hebrew text (announce) is an inner Syriac corruption.
p. 17, n. 3 Read
p. 18, n. 1 Ibn Ezra explains that naked means departing for exile or capture. Similarly Kimchi says: They will go naked into exile.
p. 18, n. 2 Rashi: For you waited for good, because you dwelt securely and prosperously, and you rebelled against the prophets.
p. 19, n. 1 Ibn Ezra: For in you were found: This is Lachish of Judea which was in the neighborhood of the tribes. The tribes learned her ways, and by her also the Daughter of Zion was influenced.

p. 19, n. 2 Kimchi: She is the beginning of the sin to the Daughter of Zion: Lachish was one of the cities of Judea. She was the first to learn the worship of Baal from Israel, because Ahab began the Baal worship. In the time of Jeroboam they did not worship the Baal but the calf, and when Ahab began the Baal worship it spread all over Israel. There was no idolatry in Judea at that time, but the inhabitants of Lachish took over Baal worship and from her it spread throughout Judea and reached even Zion (Jerusalem).

p. 19, n. 3 Kimchi: Moresheth Gath - a name of a place (Gath) in the land of the Philistines. This city is mentioned in various places. David captured it from the Philistines. Close by to Gath is found Moresheth, the meaning of which is inheritance, i.e., Gath which David captured and which later the Philistines took back from the Jews and inherited it.
p. 20, n. 1 Kimchi: That the (rich) stripped the poor, etc.

p. 21, n. 1 Kimchi: Because it is polluted: I called this your land, resting place and an inheritance, and now, because of your sins the land will not remain for you as a resting place and an inheritance. Because of your sins she will cause you to perish.
p. 21, n. 2 Ibn Ezra: Behold a man: If a man will come who will prophesy falsely, etcetera. Kimchi: ....A man who walks around in wind, i.e., his ways are ways of wind and vanity. Cf. Rashi.

p. 22, n. 1 Kimchi: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of Thee: There are some who interpret these two passages as punishment of which he speaks in the foregoing and in the following passages. And the meaning of surely I will assemble is that they will take refuge in besieged cities from fear of the foe.... The Israelites who will take refuge in the cities of the enemies will be like a flock.

p. 22, n. 2 Kimchi: And he that putteth not into their mouth: There are some who interpret this passage as meaning the bread and the meat which the false prophets receive, i.e., he who will not grant them what they ask of him in food and drink will be warred against, that is, the false prophets will gather together and will make battle with him with evil things.

p. 23, n. 1 it may mean the night; it may also refer to the verse, i.e., he quotes only two words but wants the whole verse understood. This is not the usual abbreviation in such a situation, but it should be considered here.
p. 23, n. 2 But truly I am: This the prophet says. Truly I am not like them (the false prophets).... but I am full of the holy spirit of the Lord.
p. 23, n. 3 Kimchi: The mountain of the House of the Lord: After he predicts the destruction of Zion, now, he speaks concerning the days of the Messiah and of comfort.
p. 24, n. 1 Ibn Ezra: And Thou, O tower of the flock: Yepheth (ben Ali) calls it the Tower of David, namely, Jerusalem.
p. 24, n. 2 A fairly common expression in Syriac, which means to their mind the true, monotheistic religion.
p. 25, n. 1 Kimchi: Many nations: That is Gog and Magog, and many nations that are with him.
p. 25, n. 2 Kimchi: That say, let her be defiled: They think now that Zion will be destroyed like she was formerly destroyed.
p. 25, n. 3 Peshitta has against us.
p. 26, n. 1 Ibn Ezra: And Moshe Hacohen said that here he speaks about the second Temple and the word ruler refers to Zerubabel.
p. 26, n. 2 Kimchi: This is the Messiah or Zerubabel.
p. 26, n. 3 Rashi: A travailing woman: i.e., Zion which is now in pain like a woman in labor; therefore she is called a travailing woman.
p. 27, n. 1 Rashi: They will return to Israel: They will join the remainder of the tribes, and will become one kingdom, and will not again separate into two kingdoms as before.
p. 27, n. 2 Isaiah 36, 37. 2.Kings 18:13 and chapter 19.

p. 28, n. 1 Rashi: Seven shepherds and eight princes: And our teachers, may they rest in peace, (originators of the Talmud) said: Who are the seven shepherds? David in the midst, Seth, Enoch, and Methuselah on his right side, and Abraham and Moses on his left. And who are the eight princes of men? Jesse, Saul, Samuel, Amos, Zephonia, Hezekiah, Elijah, and Messiah.
p. 28, n. 2 may mean which traces its origin (to Nimrod).
p. 28, n. 3 Read as the Peshitta and Harvard manuscripts of Bar Salibi. It seems that by error of the copyist the was misplaced by a .
p. 28, n. 4 Read
p. 29, n. 1 Jonathan Targum: And I will cut off the horses of the nations from the midst of you, and I will cause to destroy their chariots.
p. 30, n. 1 The Peshitta reads but the word given by Bar Salibi may stand for which is a less frequent contraction.

p. 31, n. 1 Ibn Ezra: He hath shewed thee: These words are the answer of the prophet. You man who asks, with what shall I appease God, and what shall I do, that I may find favor in his eyes. But he (God) does not ask of you lambs or your son, but (he asks) do justice, and do not do evil to your neighbor.
p. 31, n. 2 Jonathan Targum: Can the house of an evil person exist when it contains treasuries of falsehood?
p. 31, n. 3 Harvard manuscript adds, correctly: And destroy everything that it holds. And as in the case of him.
p. 31, n. 4 Kimchi: There will be sickenss in your bowels, and the food that you will eat will become undigestible and your appetite will not be fulfilled. Cf. Ibn Ezra.
p. 32, n. 1 Ibn Ezra: You will see how your enemies lead your sons and daughters into captivity and you will not be able to save them.
p. 32, n. 2 Similar to this is the interpretation of Kimchi: Because you blasphemed my people, i.e., the miserable, you will receive the punishment that all the nations will blaspheme you.

p. 32, n. 3 Kimchi: Woe is to me: The prophet takes part in the sorrow of his people when he sees the evil condition in which Israel finds itself, because the people did not listen to his reproaches, and now God has punished them. Therefore he says: Woe is to me for the evil that they are doing, and woe is to me because of the afflictions which have overtaken them.
p. 33, n. 1 Rashi: The great utters: the king or the elder who says when he judges in trial what he pleaseth.

p. 33, n. 2 Kimchi: The day of your watchman: the day of false prophets who are your watchmen and prophets, who gave you confidence with words of falsehood. Now you will come to see that day, whether it be good or evil.

p. 34, n. 1 Kimchi and Ibn Ezra: These are the words of the prophet in the name of Israel....: i.e., although I am exiled from my land on account of my sins, nevertheless I hope and look to God to redeem me from my exile.
